comment:
Section 3.6.4 recommends the International Patient Summary (IPS) as the cross-border exchange standard for the minimum health data set. The IPS is named without noting that SNOMED CT is the primary clinical terminology binding in the IPS specification. The HL7 FHIR IPS Implementation Guide binds clinical findings, procedures, and allergies to SNOMED CT value sets. Countries implementing IPS conformance will therefore require SNOMED CT (or GPS) for clinical coding regardless of whether the Terminology Service section makes that explicit.

This is a direct, normative dependency that should be stated. Omitting it allows a country to read §3.6.4 and the Terminology Service component description independently, without understanding that IPS conformance effectively mandates SNOMED CT.

public.suggestedRevision: Suggested addition to §3.6.4: "The IPS HL7 FHIR Implementation Guide binds key clinical elements, including problems, allergies, and procedure, to SNOMED CT value sets. Countries implementing IPS-conformant data exchange should plan for SNOMED CT (or SNOMED CT GPS for non-member countries) as the clinical terminology underpinning their IPS profiles."
